ABC News | PUBLISHED: 21 Oct 2026

ShareFollow ABC News on GoogleLONDON -- Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan who had been in Russian detention since 2022, was released Wednesday.

President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff traveled to Russia to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and oversee Hubbard's release. Witkoff landed in the Russian city of St. Petersburg on Wednesday morning, a Kremlin aide confirmed, ahead of the planned meeting with Putin.

Trump's envoy thanked Putin for freeing Hubbard, according to a readout of the meeting published by the Kremlin. Putin said that Hubbard -- who was detained in eastern Ukraine in April 2022 -- was taken to St. Peterburg's Pulkovo Airport, the readout said.

"I want to thank you very much. The president sends his thanks," Witkoff said. "Because of you, he's going home to his family."

"You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian," Witkoff told Putin. "You are a humanitarian also, sir."

Russian President Vladimir Putin shakes hands with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff during a meeting in St. Petersburg, Russia, on Oct. 21, 2026.Gavriil Grigorov/via ReutersRelatedABC News team witnesses Russia's relentless terror on Ukraine first-handHubbard's sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox, told ABC News on Wednesday that she was thanking Trump "for being the hand of God and bringing Stephen Hubbard home."

"He's been gone a long, long time. Thank you President Trump for caring for everyday Americans," she said, adding that the development was "awesome" and that the "Lord has given me peace."

US special envoy Steve Witkoff meets with Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired U.S. schoolteacher who was freed after serving a prison sentence in Russia following his conviction on mercenary charges, in Saint Petersburg, Russia, Oct. 21, 2026.ReutersFox said she had not yet spoken to her brother or to U.S. officials and that she learned about Hubbard's release from the media. Hubbard, she added, will be flown to San Antonio where there is a military base that released Americans are usually brought to for treatment.

Trump later wrote in a post to social media he asked Putin to release Hubbard in a phone call that took place last week. "Stephen is on his way back home and will soon be with his family," Trump wrote.

The U.S. "was not required to give anything in return -- an unprecedented situation for Russia," Trump added. "There was no 'swap' necessary for this release."

In this Oct. 7, 2024 file photo taken from video released by the Moscow City Court Press Service, Stephen Hubbard, a U.S. citizen accused of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine against Russia stands in a glass cage during a court session in Moscow.Moscow City Court Press Service via APThe president then posted to social media again defending his recent decision to waive numerous sanctions on Russia.

"If sanctions would have been placed, certainly those negotiations would have come to a complete and total halt," Trump wrote of the discussions over Hubbard's release.

Witkoff arrived in St. Petersburg as the Trump administration was closing in on a deal that would see multiple Americans released from detention in Russia, two U.S. officials and another source familiar with the matter told ABC News.

The talks were centered on Hubbard and several other U.S. citizens held by Moscow on what the administration believes are dubious charges, the source said.

Hubbard had been living in eastern Ukraine as a civilian since around 2014, where he taught English and had a relationship with a Ukrainian woman, according to his family.

After he was detained, Russian authorities charged Hubbard with acting as a mercenary and fighting for Ukraine, sentencing him to nearly seven years in prison. Hubbard's family and U.S. officials said the charges were false and the State Department designated him as wrongfully detained.

In this pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik, Russia's President Vladimir Putin, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov and presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev attend a meeting with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21, 2026.Kristina Solovyova/POOL/AFP via Getty ImagesRelatedTrump says what Russia is doing to Ukraine is 'fine'During their meeting, Witkoff and Putin discussed the latest U.S.-led efforts to end Moscow's ongoing invasion, which the Kremlin launched in February 2022.

"One thing that I hope to accomplish today is to have some good conversation between us about resumption potentially of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States," Witkoff said.

Special envoy Steve Witkoff speaks during his meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Konstantin Palace in Strelnya, outside St. Petersburg, Russia, Oct. 21, 2026.Kristina Solovyova/Sputnik via APWitkoff also touted U.S.-Russian "business and economic cooperation" as "an example of what the possibilities are in the future."

Witkoff traveled to St. Petersburg following a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in the Norwegian capital of Oslo on Tuesday. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb also attended the talks, which focused on ceasefire proposals to halt Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Witkoff's latest round of shuttle diplomacy comes amid intensifying White House pressure on Zelenskyy to make concessions to secure a peace deal with Moscow.

In recent weeks, Trump waived a raft of sanctions on Moscow and again blamed Kyiv for the lack of progress in U.S.-sponsored peace talks, even suggesting that Zelenskyy should be replaced as Ukrainian president.

On Tuesday, Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that the U.S. had received "nothing" for its support of Ukraine.

President Donald Trump speaks to reporters about efforts to crack down on taxpayer fraud in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, October 26, 2026.Andrew Harnik/Getty Images"Look, we have given tremendous amounts to Ukraine. We've got nothing back other than high diesel," Trump said. "We have given, probably, possibly, more money to Ukraine than almost anybody over the years, hundreds of billions of dollars. We've got nothing back, and the American taxpayers are tired of it. We want Zelenskyy to make a deal."

Following his meetings in Oslo on Tuesday, Zelenskyy said in posts to social media that he was "thankful to the American side" for its input on propose future security guarantees for Kyiv. The Ukrainian president also said he spoke with Secretary of State Marco Rubio by phone to discuss "sensitive issues such as Starlink, ballistic missile interceptors and intelligence."

On Wednesday, Zelenskyy said he continued to hold meetings in Oslo. "A lot depends on whether the American side manages to hear something new from Russia today -- about peace, not about continuing the war," he wrote.

ABC News' Joe Simonetti, Shannon K. Kingston, Fritz Farrow, Nicholas Kerr, Emily Chang, Anna Sergeeva and Justin Gomez contributed to this report.

Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan who had been in Russian detention since 2022, was released Wednesday.

Hubbard's sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox, told ABC News on Wednesday that she was thanking Trump "for being the hand of God and bringing Stephen Hubbard home."

Fox said she had not yet spoken to her brother or to U.S. officials and that she learned about Hubbard's release from the media. Hubbard, she added, will be flown to San Antonio where there is a military base that released Americans are usually brought to for treatment.

The president then posted to social media again defending his recent decision to waive numerous sanctions on Russia.

During their meeting, Witkoff and Putin discussed the latest U.S.-led efforts to end Moscow's ongoing invasion, which the Kremlin launched in February 2022.

Witkoff also touted U.S.-Russian "business and economic cooperation" as "an example of what the possibilities are in the future."

"Look, we have given tremendous amounts to Ukraine. We've got nothing back other than high diesel," Trump said. "We have given, probably, possibly, more money to Ukraine than almost anybody over the years, hundreds of billions of dollars. We've got nothing back, and the American taxpayers are tired of it. We want Zelenskyy to make a deal."
